main_reasons: Primary complexity is held-for-sale / discontinued-operations presentation of the China subsidiary (PWSH); auditor flagged it as the sole critical audit matter, but the sale closed Jan 6, 2026 for ~$51M cash, which corroborates the carrying values (gain deferred, not recognized)
Cash reconciles: continuing cash $11.2M plus held-for-sale cash $6.8M equals cash-flow ending cash $18.1M; prior year ties similarly
Continuing operations are tiny (~$0.7M revenue, mostly services) so revenue-recognition manipulation has little room; large one-off $3.0M patent sale gain is disclosed and cash-settled

Judgmental areas: modification of redeemable NCI/NCI via support agreement deemed to have no material fair-value change; goodwill $18.4M passed on qualitative test only; complex RMB-denominated temporary equity and ESOP deposit liability
Going-concern-like pressure before the sale (shareholder deficit, reverse split for Nasdaq compliance, ATM and registered direct raises), creating some incentive but no sign of aggressive accounting

Minor disclosure sloppiness (valuation allowance change $1.2M in MD&A vs $1.05M in note; 2024 tax expense described as $0.01M vs $44K; functional currency statement inconsistent with FX translation), but no restatement, no material weakness reported, clean opinion from Grant Thornton, effective ICFR assertion
